channel.title: Hui Ning · Blog
channel.description: Notes and essays on finite time, attention, AI, and biological design.

item.title: One life, and how to spend it
item.description: Remembering that life is finite changes how I weigh direction, action, and what other people think.

item.title: Where my attention actually goes
item.description: There’s no shortage of good things to read. The hard part is protecting time to figure out which questions are actually mine.

item.title: Leaving context for my future self
item.description: After a night’s sleep, I often remember the conclusion but forget how I got there. I’m trying to leave notes that let me pick right back up.

item.title: Making up my own mind
item.description: I like hearing different takes, and I want to know what kind of evidence should actually change my mind.

item.title: Getting agents to actually finish
item.description: Spell out what done looks like, keep the work moving, and have an independent reviewer inspect the real output.

item.title: AI4Bio: What happens after the prediction?
item.description: Why scaling works in biology, whether predictions survive new conditions, and which research calls models actually improve.

item.title: AI as intellectual leverage
item.description: AI changes what one person can reasonably try to build—and makes understanding the problem and judging the result matter even more.

item.title: From understanding to action
item.description: Working with AI holds up a mirror to my own habits: is the goal clear, what did acting teach me, and does my next move actually change?

item.title: When should a biological system act?
item.description: From sensing cell state in my PhD to studying immune regulation next—why I care about when biological functions turn on, how long they last, and how they shut off.
